title: सप्तषष्टितमोऽध्यायः

summary.en: Krishna says that Karna remembers dharma now, and recalls the wrongs done to Draupadi, the Pandavas and Abhimanyu without any such care. He tells Arjuna to kill the man who stood by while all of this was done.
summary.kn: ಕರ್ಣ ಈಗ ಧರ್ಮ ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಂಡಿದ್ದಾನೆಂದು ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಹೇಳಿ ದ್ರೌಪದಿ, ಪಾಂಡವರು, ಅಭಿಮನ್ಯುವಿಗೆ ಆದ ಅನ್ಯಾಯಗಳನ್ನು ಆಗ ಧರ್ಮವಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಮಾಡಿದ್ದನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಇದೆಲ್ಲಕ್ಕೆ ಸಾಕ್ಷಿಯಾಗಿ ನಿಂತವನನ್ನು ಕೊಲ್ಲಲು ಅರ್ಜುನನಿಗೆ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि कर्ण को अब धर्म याद आया है, और वे द्रौपदी, पाण्डवों और अभिमन्यु के साथ बिना इस विचार के किए गए अन्यायों को याद दिलाते हैं। वे अर्जुन से कहते हैं कि इन सबके समय साथ खड़े रहने वाले को मार दो।
summary.te: కర్ణునికి ఇప్పుడు ధర్మం గుర్తొచ్చిందని కృష్ణుడు అంటాడు; ద్రౌపది, పాండవులు, అభిమన్యునికి ఆ సమయంలో అలాంటి ఆలోచన లేకుండా చేసిన అన్యాయాలను గుర్తు చేస్తాడు. ఇదంతా జరిగినప్పుడు తోడున్నవాడిని చంపమని అర్జునునికి చెబుతాడు.
summary.ta: கர்ணனுக்கு இப்போது தர்மம் நினைவு வந்தது என்று கண்ணன் கூறி, திரௌபதி, பாண்டவர், அபிமன்யுவுக்கு அப்போது அத்தகைய எண்ணமின்றி இழைத்த அநீதிகளை நினைவூட்டுகிறார். இவையனைத்தின்போதும் உடனிருந்தவனைக் கொல்லும்படி அர்ஜுனனுக்குக் கூறுகிறார்.
summary.ml: ഇപ്പോൾ കർണ്ണൻ ധർമ്മം ഓർക്കുന്നുവെന്ന് കൃഷ്ണൻ പറയുന്നു; ദ്രൗപദിയോടും പാണ്ഡവരോടും അഭിമന്യുവിനോടും അന്ന് ഇതേ പരിഗണന കാണിക്കാതെ ചെയ്ത അനീതികളെ അദ്ദേഹം ഓർമ്മിപ്പിക്കുന്നു. ഇതെല്ലാം നടക്കുമ്പോൾ നോക്കിനിന്നവനെ കൊല്ലാൻ അദ്ദേഹം അർജുനനോട് പറയുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 8.67; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Jul 29 2019

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीद्वासुदेवो रथस्थो
राधेय दिष्ट्या स्मरसीह धर्मम् ।
प्रायेण नीचा व्यसनेषु मग्ना
निन्दन्ति दैवं कुकृतं न तत्तत् ॥

meaning.en: Then Vasudeva, standing on the chariot, said: "Radheya, how fortunate that you remember dharma now! Low people, sunk in troubles, mostly blame fate and not their own evil deeds."

verses.text:
यद्द्रौपदीमेकवस्त्रां सभाया-
मानाय्य त्वं चैव सुयोधनश्च ।
दुःशासनः शकुनिः सौबलश्च
न ते कर्ण प्रत्यभात्तत्र धर्मः ॥

meaning.en: "When you, Suyodhana, Duhshasana and Shakuni, son of Subala, brought Draupadi in a single garment into the assembly hall, Karna, where was your dharma then?"

verses.text:
यदा सभायां कौन्तेयमनक्षज्ञं युधिष्ठिरम् ।
अक्षज्ञः शकुनिर्जेता तदा धर्मः क्व ते गतः ॥

meaning.en: "When in the assembly Shakuni, skilled at dice, won against Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, who was not skilled at dice, where had your dharma gone then?"

verses.text:
यदा रजस्वलां कृष्णां दुःशासनवशे स्थिताम् ।
सभायां प्राहसः कर्ण क्व ते धर्मस्तदा गतः ॥

meaning.en: "When Krishna, in her monthly course, stood in Duhshasana's power in the assembly, you laughed at her, Karna; where had your dharma gone then?"

verses.text:
राज्यलुब्धः पुनः कर्ण समाह्वयसि पाण्डवम् ।
गान्धारराजमाश्रित्य क्व ते धर्मस्तदा गतः ॥

meaning.en: "Greedy for the kingdom, Karna, you again challenged the Pandava, relying on the king of Gandhara; where had your dharma gone then?"

verses.text:
एवमुक्ते तु राधेये वासुदेवेन पाण्डवम् ।
मन्युरभ्याविशत्तीव्रः स्मृत्वा तत्तद्धनंजयम् ॥

meaning.en: When Vasudeva had spoken so to Radheya, fierce anger entered the Pandava Dhananjaya as he remembered each of those wrongs.

verses.text:
तस्य क्रोधेन सर्वेभ्यः स्रोतोभ्यस्तेजसोऽर्चिषः ।
प्रादुरासन्महाराज तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥

meaning.en: From his anger, O great king, flames of energy came out of all the channels of his body, and it seemed a marvel.

verses.text:
तं समीक्ष्य ततः कर्णो ब्रह्मास्त्रेण धनंजयम् ।
अभ्यवर्षत्पुनर्यत्नमकरोद्रथसर्जने ।
तदस्त्रमस्त्रेणावार्य प्रजहारास्य पाण्डवः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing this, Karna showered Dhananjaya with the Brahma missile and made a further effort to bring his chariot up; but the Pandava checked that missile with a missile and struck him.

verses.text:
ततोऽन्यदस्त्रं कौन्तेयो दयितं जातवेदसः ।
मुमोच कर्णमुद्दिश्य तत्प्रजज्वाल वै भृशम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the son of Kunti loosed at Karna another missile, dear to Jatavedas, the fire god, and it blazed up greatly.

verses.text:
वारुणेन ततः कर्णः शमयामास पावकम् ।
जीमूतैश्च दिशः सर्वाश्चक्रे तिमिरदुर्दिनाः ॥

meaning.en: Then Karna quenched the fire with the Varuna missile and with rain-clouds made all quarters dark and gloomy.

verses.text:
पाण्डवेयस्त्वसंभ्रान्तो वायव्यास्त्रेण वीर्यवान् ।
अपोवाह तदाभ्राणि राधेयस्य प्रपश्यतः ॥

meaning.en: The mighty Pandava, unflustered, with the Vayavya missile carried those clouds away while Radheya looked on.

verses.text:
तं हस्तिकक्ष्याप्रवरं च बाणैः
सुवर्णमुक्तामणिवज्रमृष्टम् ।
कालप्रयत्नोत्तमशिल्पियत्नैः
कृतं सुरूपं वितमस्कमुच्चैः ॥

meaning.en: With arrows he struck down that finest banner, marked with the elephant rope, which was polished with gold, pearls, gems and diamonds, made by the best craftsmen with long and careful effort, handsome and towering, dispelling darkness.

verses.text:
ऊर्जस्करं तव सैन्यस्य नित्य-
ममित्रवित्रासनमीड्यरूपम् ।
विख्यातमादित्यसमस्य लोके
त्विषा समं पावकभानुचन्द्रैः ॥

meaning.en: It always gave energy to your army, terrified the enemies and was a splendid sight; it was famed in the world as equal to the sun, matching fire, the sun and the moon in brilliance.

verses.text:
ततः क्षुरेणाधिरथेः किरीटी
सुवर्णपुङ्खेन शितेन यत्तः ।
श्रिया ज्वलन्तं ध्वजमुन्ममाथ
महारथस्याधिरथेर्महात्मा ॥

meaning.en: Then the diadem-wearer, the great-souled Arjuna, with a sharp razor-headed arrow with a golden shaft, carefully aimed, tore down the banner of the great chariot-warrior, the son of Adhiratha, which blazed with splendor.

verses.text:
यशश्च धर्मश्च जयश्च मारिष
प्रियाणि सर्वाणि च तेन केतुना ।
तदा कुरूणां हृदयानि चापत-
न्बभूव हाहेति च निस्वनो महान् ॥

meaning.en: With that banner, my lord, fell all that was dear to the Kurus: fame, dharma and victory, and their hearts fell too; and a great cry of "Alas!" arose.

verses.text:
अथ त्वरन्कर्णवधाय पाण्डवो
महेन्द्रवज्रानलदण्डसंनिभम् ।
आदत्त पार्थोऽञ्जलिकं निषङ्गा-
त्सहस्ररश्मेरिव रश्मिमुत्तमम् ॥

meaning.en: Then, hastening to kill Karna, Partha took from his quiver an anjalika arrow, like the thunderbolt of Mahendra or the rod of fire, as if taking the finest ray of the thousand-rayed sun.

verses.text:
मर्मच्छिदं शोणितमांसदिग्धं
वैश्वानरार्कप्रतिमं महार्हम् ।
नराश्वनागासुहरं त्र्यरत्निं
षड्वाजमञ्जोगतिमुग्रवेगम् ॥

meaning.en: It split vital parts, smeared with blood and flesh, was priceless and shone like fire and the sun; it took the lives of men, horses and elephants, was three cubits long, six-feathered, straight in flight and fierce in speed.

verses.text:
सहस्रनेत्राशनितुल्यतेजसं
समानक्रव्यादमिवातिदुःसहम् ।
पिनाकनारायणचक्रसंनिभं
भयंकरं प्राणभृतां विनाशनम् ॥

meaning.en: Its energy equaled Indra's thunderbolt; it was unbearable like a flesh-eating fire, like the weapons of Pinaka and Narayana, terrifying and destroying all living beings.

verses.text:
युक्त्वा महास्त्रेण परेण मन्त्रवि-
द्विकृष्य गाण्डीवमुवाच सस्वनम् ।
अयं महास्त्रोऽप्रतिमो धृतः शरः
शरीरभिच्चासुहरश्च दुर्हृदः ॥

meaning.en: The knower of mantras fitted it to his bow with a supreme great missile, drew the sounding Gandiva and said: "This great arrow, unequaled, which I hold, will split the body and take the life of this evil-hearted man."

verses.text:
तपोऽस्ति तप्तं गुरवश्च तोषिता
मया यदिष्टं सुहृदां तथा श्रुतम् ।
अनेन सत्येन निहन्त्वयं शरः
सुदंशितः कर्णमरिं ममाजितः ॥

meaning.en: "If I have practiced austerity, pleased my elders, done what friends wished and listened as I should, by this truth let this arrow, well sharpened and unconquered, kill my enemy Karna."

verses.text:
इत्यूचिवांस्तं स मुमोच बाणं
धनंजयः कर्णवधाय घोरम् ।
कृत्यामथर्वाङ्गिरसीमिवोग्रां
दीप्तामसह्यां युधि मृत्युनापि ॥

meaning.en: Having said this, Dhananjaya loosed that terrible arrow for Karna's death, like a fierce Atharvan-Angirasa spell, blazing and unbearable in battle even to Death himself.

verses.text:
ब्रुवन्किरीटी तमतिप्रहृष्टो
अयं शरो मे विजयावहोऽस्तु ।
जिघांसुरर्केन्दुसमप्रभावः
कर्णं समाप्तिं नयतां यमाय ॥

meaning.en: The diadem-wearer, greatly delighted, said: "May this arrow, with the power of the sun and moon, bring me victory; wishing to kill Karna, may it bring him to his end for Yama."

verses.text:
तेनेषुवर्येण किरीटमाली
प्रहृष्टरूपो विजयावहेन ।
जिघांसुरर्केन्दुसमप्रभेण
चक्रे विषक्तं रिपुमाततायी ॥

meaning.en: With that excellent arrow, bringer of victory and radiant as the sun and moon, the garlanded diadem-wearer, joyful and wishing to kill, struck down the enemy who had come against him.

verses.text:
तदुद्यतादित्यसमानवर्चसं
शरन्नभोमध्यगभास्करोपमम् ।
वराङ्गमुर्व्यामपतच्चमूपते-
र्दिवाकरोऽस्तादिव रक्तमण्डलः ॥

meaning.en: Then the head of the army's leader, shining like the risen sun, like the autumn sun at midday, fell to the earth, like the red disk of the sun falling at sunset.

verses.text:
तदस्य देही सततं सुखोदितं
स्वरूपमत्यर्थमुदारकर्मणः ।
परेण कृच्छ्रेण शरीरमत्यज-
द्गृहं महर्द्धीव ससङ्गमीश्वरः ॥

meaning.en: The embodied one left that body, always happy and of great noble deeds, with great pain, as a lord of great wealth leaves a house of many attachments.

verses.text:
शरैर्विभुग्नं व्यसु तद्विवर्मणः
पपात कर्णस्य शरीरमुच्छ्रितम् ।
स्रवद्व्रणं गैरिकतोयविस्रवं
गिरेर्यथा वज्रहतं शिरस्तथा ॥

meaning.en: Broken by arrows and lifeless, the tall body of armorless Karna fell, its wounds streaming, like a mountain struck by thunderbolt, its head flowing with red ochre water.

verses.text:
देहात्तु कर्णस्य निपातितस्य
तेजो दीप्तं खं विगाह्याचिरेण ।
तदद्भुतं सर्वमनुष्ययोधाः
पश्यन्ति राजन्निहते स्म कर्णे ॥

meaning.en: From the body of the fallen Karna a blazing energy quickly rose and entered the sky; all human warriors saw that wonder, O king, when Karna was slain.

verses.text:
तं सोमकाः प्रेक्ष्य हतं शयानं
प्रीता नादं सह सैन्यैरकुर्वन् ।
तूर्याणि चाजघ्नुरतीव हृष्टा
वासांसि चैवादुधुवुर्भुजांश्च ।
बलान्विताश्चाप्यपरे ह्यनृत्य-
न्नन्योन्यमाश्लिष्य नदन्त ऊचुः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing him lie slain, the Somakas with their troops raised a joyful cry; very glad, they sounded drums, waved garments and arms, and others full of strength danced, embraced one another, shouted and spoke.

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा तु कर्णं भुवि निष्टनन्तं
हतं रथात्सायकेनावभिन्नम् ।
महानिलेनाग्निमिवापविद्धं
यज्ञावसाने शयने निशान्ते ॥

meaning.en: They saw Karna lying on the ground, groaning, slain and split by an arrow from his chariot, like a fire thrown down by a great wind, at the end of a sacrifice, on a bed at night's end.

verses.text:
शरैराचितसर्वाङ्गः शोणितौघपरिप्लुतः ।
विभाति देहः कर्णस्य स्वरश्मिभिरिवांशुमान् ॥

meaning.en: His whole body covered with arrows and drenched in streams of blood, Karna's body shone like the sun with its own rays.

verses.text:
प्रताप्य सेनामामित्रीं दीप्तैः शरगभस्तिभिः ।
बलिनार्जुनकालेन नीतोऽस्तं कर्णभास्करः ॥

meaning.en: Having scorched the enemy army with the blazing rays of his arrows, Karna, the sun, was brought to his setting by the mighty time of Arjuna.

verses.text:
अस्तं गच्छन्यथादित्यः प्रभामादाय गच्छति ।
एवं जीवितमादाय कर्णस्येषुर्जगाम ह ॥

meaning.en: As the sun, going to its setting, takes its light with it, so the arrow took Karna's life with it.

verses.text:
अपराह्णे पराह्णस्य सूतपुत्रस्य मारिष ।
छिन्नमञ्जलिकेनाजौ सोत्सेधमपतच्छिरः ॥

meaning.en: O my lord, in the afternoon, at the day's decline, the tall head of the charioteer's son, cut by the anjalika arrow in the battle, fell down.

verses.text:
उपर्युपरि सैन्यानां तस्य शत्रोस्तदञ्जसा ।
शिरः कर्णस्य सोत्सेधमिषुः सोऽपाहरद्द्रुतम् ॥

meaning.en: Over the heads of the armies, that arrow swiftly bore off the lofty head of that enemy, Karna, with ease.

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
कर्णं तु शूरं पतितं पृथिव्यां
शराचितं शोणितदिग्धगात्रम् ।
दृष्ट्वा शयानं भुवि मद्रराज-
श्छिन्नध्वजेनापययौ रथेन ॥

meaning.en: Seeing the hero Karna fallen on the ground, covered with arrows and his limbs smeared with blood, the king of the Madras, Shalya, drove away in his chariot with its banner cut down.

verses.text:
कर्णे हते कुरवः प्राद्रवन्त
भयार्दिता गाढविद्धाश्च संख्ये ।
अवेक्षमाणा मुहुरर्जुनस्य
ध्वजं महान्तं वपुषा ज्वलन्तम् ॥

meaning.en: When Karna was slain, the Kurus fled, tormented by fear and deeply wounded in the battle, looking again and again at Arjuna's great banner, blazing in its form.

verses.text:
सहस्रनेत्रप्रतिमानकर्मणः
सहस्रपत्रप्रतिमाननं शुभम् ।
सहस्ररश्मिर्दिनसंक्षये यथा
तथापतत्तस्य शिरो वसुंधराम् ॥

meaning.en: The head of him whose deeds were like those of Indra of the thousand eyes, whose fair face was like a thousand-petaled lotus, fell to the earth, like the thousand-rayed sun at day's end.
